# Translation

Then in turn Agamemnon, lord of men, addressed him:

"Son of Laertes, I rejoice to hear your speech; for you have gone through everything fittingly and set it forth. These things I am willing to swear, and my heart urges me to do so, nor will I swear falsely before the god. But let Achilles wait here for a while, eager though he be for war; and all you others, remain gathered together, until the gifts come from my hut and we cut faithful oaths. And to you yourself I give this charge and command: choosing out the best young men of all the Achaeans, bring the gifts from my ship, all that we promised yesterday to give to Achilles, and bring the women as well. And let Talthybius quickly make ready a boar for me throughout the wide army of the Achaeans, to sacrifice to Zeus and Helios."

---

*This passage is from Homer's Iliad, Book 19 (lines 184-197), where Agamemnon responds to Odysseus's counsel regarding the reconciliation with Achilles and the formal oath-taking ceremony before returning to battle.*
